conclusion.label: rejects

report:
## Conclusion: The claim is false.

The evidence overwhelmingly indicates that influenza vaccination does **not** cause Alzheimer's disease. In fact, multiple peer-reviewed studies and large cohort analyses suggest the opposite—flu vaccination is associated with a **reduced** risk of Alzheimer's disease and dementia.

### Key findings:

1. **No credible evidence supports the claim.** The Alzheimer's Drug Discovery Foundation explicitly labels this a myth, stating: "There is no peer-reviewed scientific evidence supporting this claim, instead, there is evidence to support an association between getting the flu shot and a decreased risk for dementia." ([AlzDiscovery](https://www.alzdiscovery.org/cognitive-vitality/blog/is-there-a-link-between-alzheimers-disease-and-the-flu-shot))

2. **Large studies show protective effects.** A UTHealth Houston study of nearly 2 million patients found flu vaccination linked to a **40% reduced risk** of Alzheimer's disease. ([UTHealth Houston](https://www.uth.edu/news/story/several-vaccines-associated-with-reduced-risk-of-alzheimers-disease-in-adults-65-and-older); [Medical Xpress](https://medicalxpress.com/news/2022-06-flu-vaccination-linked-alzheimer-disease.html))

3. **High-dose flu vaccine shows even stronger protection.** A 2026 Neurology study of ~200,000 adults ≥65 found high-dose influenza vaccination was associated with lower Alzheimer's risk versus standard-dose, with a stronger effect in women. ([Neurology](https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000214782); [UTHealth](https://www.uth.edu/news/story/risk-of-alzheimers-dementia-significantly-reduced-after-high-dose-influenza-vaccination-compared-to-the-standard-dose-study-finds))

4. **A systematic review of adult vaccinations** found that influenza, pneumococcal, shingles, and Tdap vaccines are all associated with lower dementia risk. ([Age & Ageing](https://academic.oup.com/ageing/article/54/11/afaf331/8339764))

The few sources suggesting a causal link (e.g., agoracosmopolitan.com, thefocalpoints.com) are not peer-reviewed and rely on non-mainstream interpretations. The weight of peer-reviewed evidence clearly refutes the claim.
